about: Open questions for the owner. type is single, multi or text. The loop adds questions here, proceeds on the default, and reads answers from .local/answers.json.

questions.title: The elevator voice: which one, and which takes?
questions.context: Listen on the Audition page (the hub address followed by /audition). Three voices read the same three lines, then the full set is in the first voice with three takes of each line. Nobody has heard any of it: the agent and Claude cannot hear. Listen for a bright, slightly slow read, sincere cheer on bad news, a genuinely flat and cold slip line, and for any take that reads a direction aloud or breaks character. Use the box for takes to swap, lines to rewrite, or a different kind of voice.

options.label: Bella
options.note: Professional, bright, warm. In the game now.

options.label: Sarah
options.note: Mature, reassuring, confident.

options.label: Brian
options.note: Deep, resonant, comforting.

options.label: None of these
options.note: Say what you want in the box.

questions.title: The Orderly after three judged rounds: what next?
questions.context: Pictures are on the Progress page. It is now its own character and sits in the room, but five blind judges across three rounds scored it between 3 and 6 out of 10 for fear, and the scores did not rise. The last judge said the X-stitched eyes look like buttons and the pastel palette looks like a toy. Building figures entirely by script seems to have a ceiling for how frightening a still picture can be.

options.label: Keep it and move on
options.note: Make it frightening through how it behaves: frozen while watched, nearer each time you look, the trolley squeak, the tape look. Revisit the model after it moves.

options.label: One more modelling pass now
options.note: Target the last judge: real sewn lids, mottled waxy skin, stained gown, a narrower grin.

options.label: Try a different way of making it
options.note: For example an AI-generated 3D sculpt or a free base mesh, re-dressed and re-rigged. Some services need an account you would have to create.

options.label: Rethink the character
options.note: Tell me what you want instead in the box.

questions.title: Waiting for the elevator: how do the blinking lights feel?
questions.context: While the car comes, the lights go out for one second every 5 to 9 seconds, with a 0.6 second warning flicker, and the Orderly moves in the dark. Try it on the Play link: earn something, go back to the elevator, press E on the call button, and wait.

options.label: The warning is too short to react to
options.note: Lengthen it to about 1.2 seconds.

options.label: One second of dark is too long
One second of dark is too short to be frightening
Standing in the car waiting for the bell is dull
options.note: Let the doors close early once everyone is aboard.

questions.title: The Orderly's first pass: what should the second pass push on?

options.label: More of a body under the gown
options.note: Ribs, spine, collarbones showing through.

options.label: Taller, so it has to duck under door frames
Make the printed smile much bigger and bolder
Something wrong where the eyes should be
Keep it absurd, the smile is the joke

questions.title: Which licence should the public repo carry?
questions.context: Your other public repos use AGPL-3.0 or MIT. With no licence, others may look but not reuse.

options.label: MIT
options.note: Anyone may reuse it, including commercially.

options.label: AGPL-3.0
options.note: Reuse must stay open source.

questions.title: Also publish a public play link on GitHub Pages?

questions.title: How many ElevenLabs characters may the game use this month?
questions.context: The account is shared with your other work. The loop checks what is left before each batch.

questions.title: Add a scheduled task that restarts the loop if the session dies?
questions.context: It would re-fire the loop every few hours, with a lock so two never run at once. It is a standing task on this PC.

options.label: Add it to the boot script

questions.title: Where will your friends be on game night?
questions.context: Playing together now works between browsers, tested on this PC only. Players connect straight to the host. Across two home networks that usually works, but some routers block it, and then that friend cannot join unless a relay service passes the traffic along. A relay needs a free account that only you can create. Tick all that apply; free text is welcome.

options.label: Everyone in one room on the same wifi
options.note: No relay needed. Nothing more to build.

options.label: Some at home: try a test with one friend first
options.note: I add a one-click connection test page you can send them. If it works, no relay is needed.

options.label: Some at home: set up a free relay so it works for everyone
options.note: I prepare everything and give you the exact sign-up steps (about five minutes). The key stays on this PC and out of the public repo.

questions.title: How should friends reach the game server?
questions.context: You said a server on your PC or the lab box is fine. I will build a small game server that keeps everyone in sync (no drawing; it runs the rules only). Your friends are outside your tailnet, so the server needs one public door. The game page itself stays on the public GitHub link; only the live game traffic goes through this door. Pick one; free text welcome.

options.label: Tailscale Funnel on one port, for the game server only
options.note: Free, no new account, gives a proper https address. You run one admin command that I give you. Only the game server is exposed, never the hub or anything else.

options.label: A Cloudflare Tunnel
options.note: Free, needs a Cloudflare account and a small program on the lab box. Hides your home address.

options.label: Open a port on my router
options.note: No account, but exposes your home address and needs a certificate for https; I would not pick this.

options.label: Friends join my tailnet
options.note: Nothing public at all, but every friend installs Tailscale and accepts an invite.

options.label: No server: keep players connecting to each other
options.note: What the game does today. Some routers will block a friend, and the host must keep the tab in front.

options.label: Keep going until Friday

options.label: Stop at the limit
options.note: It writes its report at about 3:40 on Tuesday morning and waits for you.

questions.title: Saves: keeping an old copy
questions.context: Your save sits on your own PC and the server signs it, so a hand-edited save is refused. What the signature cannot stop: someone keeps a copy from before they lost an upgrade to the roll, and puts it back before the next game night. Stopping that means the server must remember each player's latest save between nights, which means writing a small file on the lab box (today it writes nothing).

options.label: Trust your friends: allow it
options.note: Recommended. The server keeps writing nothing, and the lab box stays read-only.

options.label: The server keeps one small file of each player's latest save stamp
options.note: An old copy is refused. The container gets one writable folder.
